"""Comprehensive tests for roman.py."""

import pytest
from roman import to_roman, from_roman


# ── to_roman: basic round-trips and edge cases ────────────────────────────────

class TestToRoman:
    @pytest.mark.parametrize("n,expected", [
        (1, "I"),
        (4, "IV"),
        (5, "V"),
        (9, "IX"),
        (10, "X"),
        (40, "XL"),
        (50, "L"),
        (90, "XC"),
        (100, "C"),
        (400, "CD"),
        (500, "D"),
        (900, "CM"),
        (1000, "M"),
        (1888, "MDCCCLXXXVIII"),
        (1999, "MCMXCIX"),
        (2023, "MMXXIII"),
        (2048, "MMXLVIII"),
        (3000, "MMM"),
        (3999, "MMMCMXCIX"),
    ])
    def test_known_values(self, n, expected):
        assert to_roman(n) == expected

    @pytest.mark.parametrize("n", range(1, 4000))
    def test_roundtrip(self, n):
        """to_roman then from_roman must return the original integer."""
        assert from_roman(to_roman(n)) == n

    # ── out-of-range values ──────────────────────────────────────────────────

    @pytest.mark.parametrize("n", [0, -1, -42, 4000, 10000])
    def test_out_of_range(self, n):
        with pytest.raises(ValueError):
            to_roman(n)

    # ── non-integer types ────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    @pytest.mark.parametrize("val", [1.5, 3.14, True, False, None, "5", 5.0, []])
    def test_non_integer_raises(self, val):
        with pytest.raises(ValueError):
            to_roman(val)


# ── from_roman: valid inputs ─────────────────────────────────────────────────

class TestFromRomanValid:
    @pytest.mark.parametrize("numeral,expected", [
        ("I", 1),
        ("IV", 4),
        ("V", 5),
        ("IX", 9),
        ("X", 10),
        ("XL", 40),
        ("L", 50),
        ("XC", 90),
        ("C", 100),
        ("CD", 400),
        ("D", 500),
        ("CM", 900),
        ("M", 1000),
        ("MMMCMXCIX", 3999),
        ("MDCCCLXXXVIII", 1888),
        ("MCMXCIX", 1999),
        ("MMXXIII", 2023),
    ])
    def test_known_values(self, numeral, expected):
        assert from_roman(numeral) == expected

    @pytest.mark.parametrize("n", range(1, 4000))
    def test_roundtrip(self, n):
        """from_roman(to_roman(n)) must return the original integer."""
        assert to_roman(from_roman(to_roman(n))) == n


# ── from_roman: invalid inputs ───────────────────────────────────────────────

class TestFromRomanInvalid:
    @pytest.mark.parametrize("s", [
        "",          # empty string
        "banana",    # nonsense letters
        "IIII",      # four I's in a row
        "VV",        # repeated V
        "LL",        # repeated L
        "DD",        # repeated D
        "IC",        # invalid subtractive pair
        "XM",        # invalid subtractive pair
        "IM",        # invalid subtractive pair
        "IL",        # invalid subtractive pair
        "VM",        # invalid subtractive pair
        "VC",        # invalid subtractive pair
        "VL",        # invalid subtractive pair
        "XD",        # invalid subtractive pair
        "LC",        # invalid subtractive pair
        "DM",        # invalid subtractive pair
        "MMMM",      # four M's (4000 is out of range)
        "m",         # lowercase
        "iv",        # lowercase
        "IV ",       # trailing space
        " IV",       # leading space
        "IIII",      # too many I's
        "VVVV",      # too many V's
        "CCCC",      # too many C's
        "XXXX",      # too many X's
        "MMMM",      # too many M's
        "ABC",       # non-roman chars
        "IIX",       # non-standard subtractive
        "IIV",       # non-standard subtractive
        "A",         # single bad char
        "0",         # digit
        "1",         # digit
    ])
    def test_invalid_numerals(self, s):
        with pytest.raises(ValueError):
            from_roman(s)

    @pytest.mark.parametrize("val", [
        42,          # int instead of str
        3.14,        # float
        True,        # bool
        None,        # None
        [],          # list
        {},          # dict
    ])
    def test_non_string_raises(self, val):
        with pytest.raises(ValueError):
            from_roman(val)
